import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every method returns `app::Result<T>`, which is `Result<T, AppError>`
(`crates/sdk/src/error.rs`). An `AppError` is a **code** plus **fields**, the
shape a client receives: `{ code, message }`, with `message` the fields as a
JSON object (`{}` when there are none).

A call that fails writes nothing: the node applies a call's changes only when
it ends `Ok`, and a failed call emits no events.

## The app's own errors

Declare them once, in the `#[app::logic]` module:

```rust
#[app::error]
pub enum Error {
    NotFound,
    Taken { start: u64 },
    Invalid { reason: String },
}
```

The variant name is the code; fields keep their camelCase names, and `u64`,
`i64` and bytes are strings. Every field must have a name: a tuple variant
(`Invalid(String)`) does not compile. `Taken { start: 7 }`
reaches the client as code `Taken`, message `{"start":"7"}`. The ABI lists every
code and its fields.

Return one with `app::bail!` or `?`:

```rust
if title.is_empty() {
    app::bail!(Error::Invalid { reason: "empty title".into() });
}
self.bookings.get(&id)?.ok_or_else(|| Error::NotFound.into())
```

For an ad-hoc error, `AppError::new("Code")` or
`AppError::with_fields("Code", json!({ .. }))`; `AppError::forbidden()` and
`AppError::login_required()` are the guards' two.

## What the client receives

A failed call or view answers `422`:

| The run | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Returned an `AppError` | `422 APP_ERROR`, `details.code` the code and `details.fields` its fields |
| Trapped (a panic, out of fuel or memory, a host refusal) | `422 TRAP` |

`meroctl call` prints the node's error; a typed client turns `APP_ERROR` into
the app's own error type ([Typed clients](/build/guides/typed-clients/)).

## Errors the SDK produces

| Source | Code |
| --- | --- |
| `guards::require_member` / `require_admin` | `LoginRequired` (not an account), `Forbidden` (below the role) |
| A `Table` write | `Duplicate`, fields `{ "index": <unique constraint's name, or "key"> }` |
| Storage (encoding, limits, cursors) | `Storage`, fields `{ "message": .. }`: the `StorageError`'s text, e.g. "key is 1100 bytes, over the 1023 byte limit", "malformed cursor", "index 2 is out of bounds for length 2" |
| `files` and `std::io` | `Files`, or `Io` for other io errors |
| Cross-app calls | `Xcall` (`{ message }`), `XcallFailed` (the target's `{ code, fields }`, or `{ message }`) |
| Outbound HTTP | `Fetch` (`{ message }`) |
| Actions | `ActionView`, `ActionCall`, `StartAction` |
| Compute runs | `Compute` (`{ message }`, the host's reason) |

`StorageError`, `TableError` and `std::io::Error` convert into `AppError`, so
`?` works on every SDK call.

## Errors the dispatcher produces

Before your method runs, the generated `handle` refuses an unknown method
(`UnknownMethod`), malformed arguments (`BadArgs`), a call run as a view
(`NotAView`), a method run as the wrong kind (`WrongKind`), and a caller the
method does not allow (`Forbidden`, `LoginRequired`). The node makes the same
ABI checks before it runs the app at all, so a client normally sees them with
the node's codes; an anonymous caller of a method that is not `public` is
`401 UNAUTHENTICATED` before the app runs.

## Traps

A panic, running out of fuel or memory, or any other trap ends the run without
an app error; the call fails and writes nothing. Use errors for anything a
client should handle, and keep panics for bugs.

<Aside type="tip">
  Test failures by code: the harness's `Failure::App { code, fields }` is the
  same shape a client sees ([Testing](/build/testing/)).
</Aside>
